title: Generative Facial Expressions and Eye Gaze Behavior from Prompts for Multi-Human-Robot Interaction

fields.value: Technical/system description and proof-of-concept implementation; not experimentally validated.

quotes.text: We describe a simple zero-shot learning approach to generate facial expression and gaze shifting behaviors to control a social robot conversing with an individual or group.
The proof-of-concept generated promising results, enabling the robot’s expressions to be triggered appropriately, particularly when asked to perform a specifc gesture.
While not experimentally validated, the addition of LLM-generated nonverbal behaviors produces a perceptible improvement in the robot’s social presence.

fields.value: A robot conversing with an individual or group, with the LLM generating verbal responses containing gaze and expression tags. No participant study task is reported.

quotes.text: We describe a simple zero-shot learning approach to generate facial expression and gaze shifting behaviors to control a social robot conversing with an individual or group.
To demonstrate this, we describe a proof-of-concept implementation using the robot Furhat.

fields.value: No measured outcomes or statistical results are reported; the authors describe a perceptible improvement in social presence, while noting the approach was not experimentally validated.

fields.value: The paper frames gaze as a nonverbal cue that conveys intent, regulates conversation, fosters engagement, and helps robots manage attention in multiparty interactions. It operationalizes robot gaze through gaze shifting and breaking eye contact.

quotes.text: Nonverbal cues such as eye gaze and facial expressions play critical roles in conveying intent, regulating conversation, and fostering engagement.

In multi-human-robot interactions, even more nuanced behavior from robots is required to effectively manage attention, maintain a sense of inclusion among participants, and adapt to the dynamic nature of group interactions.

fields.value: A prompt instructs GPT-3.5 to generate conversational responses with embedded tags for gaze shifts and facial gestures. Furhat user detection triggers the interaction; the system parses the response into speech and gesture tags, generates speech with Azure Neural voices, recognizes user speech with Google Cloud Speech-to-Text, and repeats the cycle. The authors note user detection is limited to two people.

quotes.text: To design a simple prompt to guide eye gaze and gestures during conversation, we specified four distinct parts: Characterization Description of role or perspective the LLM should take when replying.
The OpenAI Completion class was used to create a response using the Davinci-3 variant of GPT-3.5 [22], 2048 maximum tokens, and a temperature of 0.7.
The returned response was parsed into a sequence of sentences intended for verbalization and embedded gesture tags.

fields.value: Furhat, an embodied conversational robot. The paper cites Furhat as a back-projected human-like robot head.

quotes.text: To demonstrate this, we describe a proof-of-concept implementation using the robot Furhat.
Furhat: A Back-Projected Human-Like Robot Head for Multiparty Human-Machine Interaction.

fields.value: The paper presents a proof-of-concept in which an LLM uses prompt instructions to add gaze shifts and facial-expression tags to a Furhat robot’s conversational responses. The authors describe the behavior as improving social presence, but report no experimental validation or measured participant outcomes.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper frames gaze as a nonverbal behavior for managing attention, inclusion, engagement, and conversational regulation; it describes an LLM-based implementation on Furhat and makes an unvalidated claim about social presence. It does not report empirical effects or address how embodiment influences study findings.
